title: HfO2/MgF2 Quarter-Wave Stack with Bounded Thickness Optimization
scientific_hypothesis: A 29-layer alternating HfO2/MgF2 stack with thicknesses constrained to [30, 150] nm and regularized toward quarter-wave values at 267.5 nm center wavelength will achieve higher target scores than unconstrained thickness optimization, while maintaining physical validity.
design_principle: Quarter-wave stacks produce high reflectance outside the design wavelength through Bragg interference. By centering the quarter-wave condition at 267.5 nm (midpoint of 255-280 nm passband), the stack should transmit the UV band while reflecting visible and NIR. Thickness bounds prevent non-physical excursions that waste optimization budget.
proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | SiO2 substrate (29 layers total, starting with HfO2)
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 29 layers, bounded to [30, 150] nm
L2 regularization weight toward theoretical quarter-wave thickness (λ/4n_i) at 267.5 nm
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 255-280 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 300-700 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 700-1100 nm band
Maintain thickness smoothness between adjacent layers
manufacturing_considerations: 29 layers is within the 30-layer maximum constraint
HfO2 and MgF2 are conventional evaporable/sputterable dielectrics
Thickness bounds [30, 150] nm are within typical deposition control capability
theory_basis: Recalled: Quarter-wave stacks produce stopbands centered at the design wavelength with bandwidth proportional to the index contrast ratio
Recalled: HfO2 has higher refractive index (~2.0-2.2) than MgF2 (~1.38-1.42) in the UV, providing adequate index contrast
Recalled: Fused silica (SiO2) is transparent down to ~180 nm and is a standard UV substrate
Recalled: Layer thicknesses near λ/4n produce maximum reflectance at the design wavelength for Bragg stacks
Recalled: Bounding thickness optimization prevents convergence to non-fabricable designs and reduces search space dimension
expected_advantages: Tighter thickness bounds should reduce optimizer wandering and improve convergence speed
L2 regularization toward quarter-wave values should keep the stack near the physically-intended interference condition
Maintaining the same material pair and layer count isolates thickness tuning as the only variable axis
Continuation from iteration_07 allows direct comparison of constraint effects on the same topology
known_risks: Uncertain: Exact n/k values for HfO2 and MgF2 at 255-280 nm from the local registry -- recalled values are ~2.0-2.2 and ~1.38-1.42 respectively but registry data may differ
Uncertain: Whether 29 layers is optimal or if fewer layers would achieve similar performance with better robustness -- this route does not explore layer count
Uncertain: Whether HfO2/MgF2 is the best material pair for this UV band -- Al2O3/MgF2 or other combinations were not explored
Risk: L2 regularization may over-constrain the optimizer if the ideal solution deviates from quarter-wave due to dispersion
Risk: Thickness bounds [30, 150] nm may exclude valid solutions -- quarter-wave at 267.5 nm for HfO2 (n~2.0) is ~33 nm and for MgF2 (n~1.4) is ~48 nm, so lower bound is tight
execution_request_english: Design a 29-layer planar multilayer thin-film filter on a fused silica (SiO2 (Gao)) substrate with air incidence. The stack alternates HfO2 and MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) layers, starting with HfO2 adjacent to air and ending with MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) adjacent to the substrate. Optimize all 29 layer thicknesses with hard bounds of [30, 150] nm per layer. Apply L2 regularization penalty targeting theoretical quarter-wave thickness at 267.5 nm center wavelength (thickness_target_i = 267.5 / (4 * n_i) where n_i is the refractive index of the layer material at 267.5 nm). Maximize transmittance in 255-280 nm band, minimize transmittance in 300-700 nm band, and minimize transmittance in 700-1100 nm band. Use coherent transfer matrix method solver with normal incidence, unpolarized light. No metal layers. Total layer count is exactly 29. Material names must resolve to hfo2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), and SiO2 (Gao) from the registry.
revision_reason: Continuation from iteration_07: enforcing hard thickness bounds [30, 150] nm and L2 regularization toward quarter-wave values to suppress exploratory overshoot and accelerate convergence into the physically-intended thin-film regime, per feedback directives.
